scenes.name: before-after
scenes.alt: Animated illustration, before and after. Before: six cards pile up. Every bus broadcasts SSID001 and the tablet joins whichever is loudest. The display on bus 12 talks to the router in bus 14, parked next to it. The OS says connected and nothing says it is the wrong BSSID. The link drops at a stop and nobody reconnects it. Someone walks over and picks the network in Settings again. After a reboot the device only remembers the name. A wipe turns the label to After: an app log runs "await manager.start()", loads SSID001 at aa:bb:cc:00:00:02, requests that BSSID only, joins and verifies it, and ends on connected, isVerified true. Five outcomes appear: pick the router by BSSID from a scan, Android joins only that BSSID, every join is checked and a mismatch is released, the router is saved after the check and restored by start, and a lost link retries at 2, 4, 8, 16, then 30 seconds.

scenes.name: how-it-works
scenes.alt: Animated diagram of four steps, left to right. 1, scan: ScanWifi on Android, one row per BSSID, strongest signal first. 2, join one BSSID: connectNew with the config, Android uses WifiNetworkSpecifier, iOS joins by SSID. 3, highlighted, verify and save: read the BSSID actually joined, on a mismatch release it and report, on a match save the router. 4, stay on it: app traffic bound to the network on Android, a lost link retries from 2 to 30 seconds, start restores it on the next launch. Below, a loop line: link dropped? WifiManagement retries the stored router, one attempt at a time, until it verifies again.

data.title: How it works
